body_markdown:
*The Manchester physiotherapist and former Race Across the World contestant was remembered by her family as a courageous, adventurous and deeply loving woman.*


Jo Gardiner, who became known to millions of viewers through the BBC travel series *Race Across the World* , has died at the age of 61 following a long battle with cancer.


Gardiner appeared on the second series of the popular travel competition alongside her son, Sam. Her death comes only a year after Sam died in a road accident at the age of 24, leaving the family facing another devastating loss.


Her family confirmed her death in a statement, describing her as an adventurous, brave and loving person whose energy and personality had a lasting impact on everyone around her.


## A life remembered for adventure


Gardiner was a physiotherapist from Manchester and was known by those close to her for her enthusiasm for life and willingness to embrace new experiences.


For television viewers, one of her most memorable adventures came in 2020, when she and Sam took part in the second series of *Race Across the World* . The pair travelled across South America as they competed against other teams in a race covering thousands of miles.


The contestants began their journey in Mexico City and aimed to reach Ushuaia in Argentina without relying on flights. Instead, they had to navigate unfamiliar places using public transport and other forms of travel while managing limited resources.


For Gardiner, the experience was about much more than competition. It gave her the opportunity to share an extraordinary journey with her son and create memories that would later become particularly precious to the family.


The programme also introduced viewers to the close relationship between mother and son. Their journey showed moments of humour, frustration, determination and affection as they attempted to overcome the challenges placed in front of them.


Gardiner's family said she had a special ability to make people feel valued and connected. They remembered her as someone whose personality could bring people together and make ordinary experiences feel memorable.


## A devastating loss for the family


Gardiner's death follows the tragic death of her son Sam in June 2025.


Sam, a landscape gardener, was 24 when his Volkswagen Golf R estate left the road and overturned. He had been working on an isolated estate on Scotland's west coast and had returned to Manchester for a family gathering.


His death came several years after audiences had watched him and his mother travel together on *Race Across the World* .


The loss was particularly painful because of the strong bond between the pair. Their television journey had allowed viewers to see the relationship between a mother and son as they faced unfamiliar countries and demanding circumstances together.


Following Sam's death, the programme's production team paid tribute to both Gardiner and her son, recognising the important contribution they had made to the second series.


Their appearance had remained memorable for fans of the programme, with many viewers remembering their determination and warmth throughout the journey.


## Tributes from Race Across the World


The *Race Across the World* team has paid tribute to Gardiner following news of her death.


A spokesperson for the programme said the production team, the BBC and the wider cast were deeply saddened by her passing. They also remembered the impact that both Jo and Sam had on the series.


Gardiner was described as a figure who had become almost like a matriarch within the programme's wider family.


The statement highlighted her passion for life, kindness and strength, while also recalling the devotion she showed towards her family.


The team said the memories created during the pair's journey across Latin America would remain important to those who worked on the series and to the viewers who followed their story.


## Her family's tribute


In their statement, Gardiner's family remembered her not only as an adventurer but also as the heart of their family.


They said she had been surrounded by many friends and had a remarkable ability to make people feel as though they were among the most important people in her life.


They also asked those who knew her to remember her through laughter, stories and adventure.


Rather than focusing only on grief, the family encouraged people to celebrate the way Gardiner lived. They recalled her courage, kindness, humour and enthusiasm, qualities that they said would continue through the people whose lives she had touched.


Gardiner is survived by her son Charlie.


Her family has also established a JustGiving fundraising page in her memory, with donations supporting Diabetes UK. Gardiner lived with type 1 diabetes and had worked as an ambassador for the charity.


## A memorable television journey


The second series of *Race Across the World* was filmed before the coronavirus pandemic and later became one of the programmes that helped establish the format as a major BBC entertainment series.


Gardiner and Sam's participation gave viewers a chance to see a family relationship tested by long journeys, unfamiliar environments and the pressures of competition.


Their story has taken on a deeper significance following Sam's death and now Gardiner's passing.


For fans who watched the pair cross South America, their time on the programme represents more than a television competition. It captured a mother and son sharing an unusual experience together and making memories that their family will now carry forward.


Gardiner's death marks the loss of a woman remembered for embracing life despite the challenges she faced.


Her family has asked for privacy as they mourn, while encouraging those who knew her to celebrate the qualities that made her distinctive.


Through her work, friendships, charitable efforts and television appearance, Gardiner touched the lives of many people. Her journey with Sam also left a lasting impression on *Race Across the World* viewers.


At a time of profound loss, the family's message is ultimately one of remembrance. Gardiner is being remembered not simply for the illness that ended her life, but for the adventures she pursued, the people she loved and the joy she brought to those around her.


For viewers who first encountered her on television, Jo Gardiner will remain associated with courage, curiosity and a willingness to make the most of every opportunity.


### Source


*The Independent* on 24 August 2026.
